# CLI reference

Every GTM Toolkit command, argument and option, generated from the CLI: init, validate, lint, build, check, coverage, diff, rules and explain.

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-docs.mjs from `gtm reference`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command of GTM Toolkit 2.0.0, printed from the CLI itself.

```bash
npx gtm <command> [options]
```

Exit codes are the same everywhere: `0` clean, `1` findings (errors, or more warnings than `--max-warnings` allows), `2` the command was used wrongly.

## Global options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-v, --version` | output the version number |
| `-C, --cwd <dir>` | run as if started in this directory |
| `--dir <dir>` | spec directory, relative to the project root |

## init

Scaffold a gtm/ spec in this project. Never overwrites a file.

```bash
gtm init [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` | site or product name |  |
| `--url <url>` | canonical site origin, for example https://www.example.dev |  |
| `--description <text>` | one or two sentences on what this is |  |
| `--minimal` | write gtm.yaml only, without the strategy files |  |

## validate

Check the spec: schema, references between files, claims without proof.

```bash
gtm validate [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f, --format <format>` | stylish, json or github | `stylish` |

## lint

Check content against the spec: SEO structure, vocabulary, references, links.

```bash
gtm lint [options] [paths...]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[paths...]` | files or folders to report on (default: every collection) |

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f, --format <format>` | stylish, json or github | `stylish` |
| `--changed [base]` | only files changed against a git ref (default: origin/HEAD) or not yet committed |  |
| `--max-warnings <n>` | exit 1 when there are more warnings than this |  |
| `--quiet` | report errors only |  |

## build

Compile the spec and content into robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, GTM.md and JSON-LD.

```bash
gtm build [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | write nothing; exit 1 if a generated file is missing or stale |  |
| `--dry-run` | show what would change without writing |  |
| `-f, --format <format>` | stylish, json or github | `stylish` |

## check

validate + lint + build --check in one pass. The command to run in CI.

```bash
gtm check [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f, --format <format>` | stylish, json or github | `stylish` |
| `--max-warnings <n>` | exit 1 when there are more warnings than this |  |
| `--quiet` | report errors only |  |

## coverage

Strategy against execution: published content per persona, topic, pillar and question.

```bash
gtm coverage [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f, --format <format>` | stylish, json or md | `stylish` |

## diff

What changed in the strategy since a git ref, and which content it strands.

```bash
gtm diff [options] [base]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[base]` | git ref to compare the working tree against |

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f, --format <format>` | stylish, json or md | `stylish` |

## rules

List the content rules and their current severity.

```bash
gtm rules [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f, --format <format>` | stylish or json | `stylish` |

## explain

Say what a rule checks and why it exists.

```bash
gtm explain [options] <rule>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<rule>` | rule id, for example seo/internal-links |
